(d) line 210 is the `for k, v in params.items()` head; it is RE-VISITED once per iteration (loop continuations land on this line again). (e) line 211 evaluates `isinstance(v, dict)`; when truthy, the multi-line statement at 212-216 computes the md5-digest hex fragment. CPython tracing typically emits ONE line event at line 212 for the start of that compound expression and may also emit events on the continuation lines (213-216). When `isinstance` is FALSE, lines 212-216 are SKIPPED entirely. (f) lines 217 and 218 (the two `re.sub` calls) ALWAYS execute on every iteration regardless of the dict branch. (g) after the for loop exits, line 220 evaluates `isinstance(s, str_node)`. The crafted input is a plain `str`, so line 221 is NOT visited. (h) line 223 is the final `return`. - 205 assigns the regex pattern.
- 206 checks `if not re.search(pattern, s)`.
- Because the input string contains `${...}` and `&{...}`, that condition is false, so 207 is skipped.
- 209 deep-copies `s`.
- 210 is the `for k, v in params.items()` loop head, revisited for each iteration and once more when the loop terminates.
- 211 checks whether each value is a dict.
- For dict values, 212–216 compute `v` as the first four hex chars of the MD5 digest of `json.dumps(v).encode("utf-8")`.
- 217 and 218 always run each iteration.
- 220 checks `isinstance(s, str_node)`. The test passes a plain Python string literal, so 221 is skipped.
- 223 returns the tuple.

3. `Env` -> string, so again 211 false, then 217, 218.
4. `Owner` -> dict, same dict branch as `Cfg`, then 217, 218.
After the last iteration, control returns to 210 once more, then exits loop to 220 and 223.
